page.layout: One page of text in two columns; running head at top; margin notes at the right edge (Cicero, Oratore; Orosius; Lib. I; Cap. II) and at the left edge; a centred heading "SACRA." between the two parts; marginal references beside the second column (2. Maccab. 4.5; Iosephus; Esr. 10.17); a note at the foot of the second column.

main_text.p: parcens. Jugulatus est ab Alexandro Rege Syro; Leonidas Rhodius, qui primus & solus in quatuor Olympiadibus duodecies coronatus est. Carneades Philosophus Academicus, quamvis memoriae ufus, tanto apparatu ad confutandas quae Zeno fcripferat, aggrefsus est, ut fuperiora capitis helle- boro candido, ne quid ex corruptis in stomacho humoribus ad domicilium animi redundaret, purgaret. Intra hoc etiam tempus hyems adeò rigida fuit, ut arbores cunctas deureret; Pelles Rhenus adeo graffabatur, ut Libitina nec libero- rum quidem funeribus sufficeret, fervorum cadavera publice abjicerentur, nec tamen tangerent- tur à brutis. Pomptinae paludes à Cethego Conf. fiscatae & ager ex iis factus est.
main_text.head: SACRA.
main_text.p: In JVDAICA Ecclesia duo occurrunt, nempe duplex sub Antiocho instituta persecutio & Fortificatus; In prima illarum templum & pol- luvit, conferendi sacerdoti jus ad se traduxit, aliquie suis affectis vendidit Antiochus. In sc- Joseph l. 12 cando super bafi altaris Domini idoleum collo- cavit, bibliorum codicem exuffit, pueros cir- cumcidi vetuit, ac Judaeis Dijs Graecorum facta facere, Samaritanis id non refragantibus, cocgit. Pontifices intra hoc tempus mira fortunae vicissitudine fuere plures; Onias, Jason, Menelaus, Jesus & Jonathas Onias Senior ab Antiocho, in- gante & CCC Talenta offerente Jason *, de- posit est. Jasonem (seu Jesum), Onias ī-cu Menelaus Junior frater, illā pecunia fuo nomine oblata

page.notes: Marginal notes: Cicero, Orator (right, top); Orosius, Lib. I, cap. II (right); Livius, Lib. 40 (right); 2. Maccab. 4.5 and Ioseph. l. 12 c. 17 (right, second column). Left-margin notes are largely cut off and illegible. Several words in the first column are partly obscured by show-through and ink damage; readings are doubtful, especially in names (Carneades, Jason, Menelaus). Greek words in the margin and some of the Greek-letter references are not legible enough to transcribe.
